context.guidance: Protect each Tier A and Tier B Personal Data Element at field or column level before it is stored, with keys held outside the data store, so that a database dump or a restored backup does not reveal the values. Disk or volume encryption protects only the storage medium, so it lowers severity without clearing the Finding. Until DPDP §44(2) omits IT Act §43A, that section's reasonable-security duty applies alongside Rule 6(1)(a).

value.fix: Encrypt the «SECRET» column at the field level before it is persisted. Use AES-256-GCM with a random 96-bit IV per value, store the ciphertext, IV, and auth tag together (e.g., as base64 in a TEXT column), and load the key from a KMS, HSM, or secrets manager, never from the database or the repo. Implement this in the Sequelize model with getter/setter methods or hooks so every write is encrypted and every read is decrypted. Change the column type from STRING to TEXT to fit ciphertext, and replace defaultValue '' with null, or encrypt the empty string so the default is not stored in plaintext. Write a migration that encrypts existing rows and then drops the plaintext. Add key rotation with a key ID stored alongside each ciphertext. Confirm that a DB dump or restored backup contains only ciphertext, and that the key is not stored in it. Disk or volume encryption alone does not satisfy this finding.
